prompt: what subjects (including linguistic and programming languages) i need to study, learn and practice in order to design a high speed pcb capable to connect a sodimm ddr4 ram stick to a pci express x16 3.0 and prevent any problem of drop in the ram's performance, and design a way to make the ram communicate with the pci port.
judge_reasoning: Candidate 1 is the most aligned with the prompt: it directly lists the kinds of subjects to study (memory interface standards, PCIe, high-speed PCB/signal integrity, FPGA/ASIC, drivers) and frames them toward building a DDR4 (SO-DIMM) to PCIe x16 communications/bridge approach. Candidate 2 is largely generic high-speed PCB engineering guidance and doesn’t address the specific DDR4-to-PCIe interface/communication problem. Candidate 3 focuses on general DDR4 vs PCIe background and broad optimization, but it never meaningfully answers the “make the RAM communicate with the PCIe port” requirement. Candidate 4 mainly enumerates simulation/measurement tools for high-speed PCBs, with little relevance to the core integration/subject-learning goals.
